nodes.name: Strategic radiation-hardened processor / FPGA / memory
nodes.description: The concentrated, export-sensitive corner of launch/space avionics: true rad-hard general-purpose processors, rad-hard/rad-tolerant FPGAs, and rad-hard memory for the harshest GEO/deep-space radiation environments. This is the chokepoint axis (few trusted foundries, long lead times), distinct from the COTS-upscreened path that high-cadence launchers like Falcon 9 mostly use for ascent avionics. Suppliers cluster on a handful of Western houses (BAE RAD750/RAD5545, Frontgrade/Microchip, AMD/Xilinx, plus the DoD-funded SkyWater RH90 trusted foundry).
nodes.notes: Honesty split (brief §3): this node is the STRATEGIC rad-hard corner (concentrated). Falcon 9 ascent avionics largely use COTS-upscreened silicon (commodity, broad supply) captured separately in launch_cots_upscreened_avionics_silicon. Strategic rad-hard is the corner traditional GPS/defense/GEO sat primes depend on.

nodes.name: COTS-upscreened avionics silicon (Falcon-class)
nodes.description: The commodity counterweight to strategic rad-hard: commercial-off-the-shelf silicon (e.g. dual-core x86) selected, radiation-characterized, acceptance-tested, and protected by triple modular redundancy, ECC, scrubbing, and watchdogs rather than paying the full rad-hard premium. This is how SpaceX Falcon-class ascent avionics achieves radiation tolerance with broad commercial supply, so the silicon supply here is NOT a single-source chokepoint. SpaceX's avionics design itself is captive (must_build); the underlying parts are commodity.
nodes.notes: Brief honesty call: distinguishes COTS-upscreened (commodity, broad supply, captive architecture) from strategic rad-hard (concentrated corner). Recall is NOT earned by pretending captive COTS-upscreened avionics has a public single-source supplier.

nodes.name: Space-grade IMU / inertial reference / GNSS
nodes.description: Inertial measurement / reference units (ring-laser-gyro, hemispherical-resonator-gyro, FOG, MEMS) plus GNSS receivers that feed the fault-tolerant GNC loop and the autonomous flight-safety position solution. The high-reliability space-grade IMU/gyro tier is concentrated on two dominant Western houses (Honeywell MIMU, Northrop Grumman SIRU/HRG), with Safran and Northrop-LITEF MEMS as lower-cost adjacents; modern launchers can also blend tactical-grade MEMS upscreened parts.

nodes.name: Star tracker / stellar attitude sensor
nodes.description: Optical stellar-reference sensors for precise attitude determination on upper stages, spacecraft, and (increasingly) constellation buses. The merchant star-tracker market is led by Sodern (ArianeGroup), with Jena-Optronik (Airbus) and Ball/BAE as the other established high-reliability suppliers; New Space mega-constellation demand has pulled in higher-rate, lower-cost variants. More relevant to payload/spacecraft attitude than to Falcon-9 ascent, but a core GNC sensor for the broader reusable-launch + on-orbit chain.

nodes.name: Space-grade connectors & flight harness (launch vehicle)
nodes.description: Launch-vehicle avionics interconnect: ruggedized circular/rectangular connectors, hermetics, and shielded harness rated for vibration, thermal cycling, outgassing, and radiation. Supply is broad but quality-concentrated on a few interconnect houses (Glenair, TE/DEUTSCH, Amphenol). Distinct from the orbital-data-center connector node; this is the ascent/recovery harness on the reusable stack.

nodes.name: Flight-termination ordnance & safe-and-arm devices
nodes.description: The energetic / ordnance half of the autonomous flight-safety system: safe-and-arm devices, initiators, and destruct charges that the onboard AFTS computer commands. The flight-safety DECISION computer is SpaceX-captive (custom AFTS), but the qualified safe-and-arm / ordnance hardware is a concentrated merchant corner dominated by Pacific Scientific Energetic Materials (PacSci EMC, a Fortive subsidiary), the established U.S. supplier of safe-and-arm / arm-fire devices flown on most U.S. launch vehicles.
nodes.notes: Honesty: AFTS decision/control electronics are SpaceX-captive (see autonomous_flight_safety_system + spaceflightnow AFSS evidence). The merchant exposure is the safe-and-arm / ordnance hardware, not the flight-safety software.

nodes.name: BAE Systems
nodes.description: British defense/aerospace prime and the heritage leader in strategic radiation-hardened space processors (RAD750 at 150nm, RAD5545 at 45nm; 12nm rad-hard library in development). Its single-board computers are the long-standing workhorse of high-reliability space computing. BAE also absorbed Ball Aerospace (2024) bringing the CT-2020 rad-hard star tracker. Listed on the London Stock Exchange.
nodes.notes: Strategic rad-hard processor corner. ticker BA.L verified via London Stock Exchange listing 2026-06.

nodes.name: Frontgrade Technologies
nodes.description: Self-described largest provider of analog and radiation-hardened electronics for the aerospace, defense, and medical industries; portfolio spans rad-hard FPGAs, memory, microprocessors, mission-processing subsystems, ASICs, and power management. Formerly Cobham Advanced Electronic Solutions (CAES); owned by Veritas Capital, so privately held (no public ticker).
nodes.notes: Private (Veritas Capital), formerly CAES. No public ticker; do not guess. Strategic rad-hard supplier.

nodes.name: Microchip Technology
nodes.description: U.S. semiconductor maker and one of the two dominant space-grade FPGA suppliers. Its RTG4 rad-tolerant FPGAs are hardened by design against single-event upsets for LEO/MEO/GEO/HEO/deep-space, and its RT PolarFire FPGA is QML Class Q qualified for spaceflight. Listed on Nasdaq (MCHP).
nodes.notes: ticker MCHP (Nasdaq). One of two dominant space FPGA houses (with AMD/Xilinx). Distinct company from Frontgrade despite seed lumping them.

nodes.name: AMD (Xilinx)
nodes.description: Owner of the former Xilinx space-grade FPGA line and the other of the two dominant space-FPGA suppliers. Space-grade XQR Kintex UltraScale (20nm, flying on Mars Perseverance) and the newer radiation-tolerant XQR Versal adaptive SoC (Class B qualified, shipping from early 2023, reprogrammable in-flight) anchor high-performance on-board processing. Listed on Nasdaq (AMD).
nodes.notes: ticker AMD (Nasdaq); acquired Xilinx 2022. Second of two dominant space FPGA houses.

nodes.name: SkyWater Technology
nodes.description: U.S.-owned pure-play silicon foundry and DMEA Cat-1A Trusted Foundry; recipient of DoD funding (up to $170M, then +$99M in Sept 2022) to broaden onshore production of strategic radiation-hardened (RH90, 90nm) electronics. Represents the policy-driven onshore-capacity build for the strategic rad-hard corner. Listed on Nasdaq (SKYT).
nodes.notes: ticker SKYT (Nasdaq). From .eval dev set (rl_dev_radhard_microelectronics_skywater_2019_2022). Trusted-foundry RH90 onshore capacity.

nodes.name: Northrop Grumman
nodes.description: U.S. aerospace/defense prime and the other dominant space-grade inertial house via its Scalable Space Inertial Reference Unit (SIRU) family, built on hemispherical resonator gyro (HRG) technology that has logged 50 million on-orbit hours without a single mission failure aboard more than 200 spacecraft, and is naturally radiation-hardened by its quartz construction. Its LITEF subsidiary supplies MEMS/FOG IMUs. Listed on NYSE (NOC).
nodes.notes: ticker NOC (NYSE). HRG/SIRU = second dominant space IMU/gyro corner alongside Honeywell.

nodes.name: Sodern
nodes.description: French optronics maker and self-described world leader in star trackers, offering the most extensive range on the market (Hydra, Auriga families) with extensive flight heritage from LEO to deep space; Auriga units equip large LEO communications constellations. A subsidiary of ArianeGroup (a privately held Airbus/Safran joint venture), so no public ticker of its own.
nodes.notes: Subsidiary of ArianeGroup (private Airbus/Safran JV). No standalone public ticker; do not guess. Market-leading star-tracker corner.

nodes.name: Jena-Optronik
nodes.description: German maker of star sensors / attitude-orbit-control sensors and, with Sodern, one of the two established European star-tracker houses. Its ASTRO APS is described as the world's most successful and extensively used high-reliability satellite attitude-orbit-control sensor; the compact rad-hard ASTRO CL targets small satellites and mega-constellations. A subsidiary of Airbus Defence and Space (Airbus SE, Euronext Paris AIR.PA).
nodes.notes: Subsidiary of Airbus Defence and Space; parent Airbus SE ticker AIR.PA (Euronext Paris). Second established European star-tracker house.

nodes.name: Glenair
nodes.description: U.S. interconnect maker specializing in miniaturized, weight-critical space connectors and harness. Its Series 80 Mighty Mouse is specified on hundreds of mission-critical interconnect applications worldwide and has become the de facto high-performance connector solution for former MIL-DTL-38999 users, at roughly half the size and weight. Glenair delivers complete launch-vehicle avionics interconnect systems with proven flight heritage. Privately held.
nodes.notes: Private company (no public ticker; do not guess). Concentrated launch-harness interconnect supplier.

nodes.name: Pacific Scientific Energetic Materials (PacSci EMC)
nodes.description: U.S. ordnance/energetics maker and the established supplier of safe-and-arm / arm-fire devices, initiators, and flight-termination ordnance for space launch vehicles, with hardware flown across most U.S. launch programs. A subsidiary of Fortive Corporation (NYSE: FTV).
nodes.notes: Subsidiary of Fortive (confirmed via SEC EDGAR Fortive 10-K subsidiaries list); parent ticker FTV (NYSE). Concentrated FTS/ordnance corner.

nodes.name: Moog Inc.
nodes.description: U.S. precision motion-control and systems integrator whose high-performance systems control launch vehicles, satellites, and space vehicles; in avionics it supplies space-grade payload-processing single-board computers (e.g. radiation-tolerant SpaceVPX GPU/FPGA boards) and control-surface/actuation electronics. Listed on NYSE (MOG.A).
nodes.notes: ticker MOG.A (NYSE). Board-level / actuation-electronics integrator (reported_capable_supplier), not a silicon maker.

nodes.name: Mercury Systems
nodes.description: U.S. defense-electronics maker that builds space-qualified FPGA processing boards (including the first space-qualified board powered by AMD Xilinx Versal technology), integrating merchant rad-tolerant silicon into flight processing subsystems. A board-level integrator rather than a chip maker. Listed on Nasdaq (MRCY).
nodes.notes: ticker MRCY (Nasdaq). Board integrator (reported_capable_supplier) of AMD/Xilinx Versal into space processing boards. Mercury IR page timed out; evidence sourced from WebSearch-surfaced verbatim (paywalled_snippet).

edges.claim: Strategic rad-hard processors/FPGAs/memory are the concentrated-supply component within fault-tolerant launch/space avionics.
COTS-upscreened, triple-redundant silicon is the commodity path Falcon-class ascent avionics uses for radiation tolerance, distinct from strategic rad-hard.
Space-grade IMU / inertial reference / GNSS feeds the fault-tolerant GNC loop.
Star trackers provide stellar attitude reference within the GNC sensor suite.
Space-grade connectors and flight harness interconnect the avionics on the reusable launch stack.
Safe-and-arm / ordnance hardware is the energetic component the autonomous flight-safety system commands.
BAE Systems is the heritage leader in strategic rad-hard space processors (RAD750 150nm, RAD5545 45nm); long-standing go-to in high-reliability radiation-hardened space computing.
edges.context: Capability/heritage supplier to the broad reusable-launch + space industry; not asserted as a confirmed SpaceX Falcon BOM item.

Microchip RTG4 / RT PolarFire are space-qualified rad-tolerant FPGAs; one of the two dominant space-FPGA suppliers.

evidence.title: Breaking Defense: BAE Systems rad-hard space processors (RAD750 / RAD5545)
evidence.excerpt: the RAD750® single board computer from the same basic product family that was on Curiosity, and has been the 'go to' solution in high-reliability radiation hardened computing in space for the last 20 years.
evidence.summary: Steve 'Doogie' Russell, BAE Systems Space Systems Lead, on the RAD750 as the 20-year go-to in high-reliability rad-hard space computing, and the RAD5545 as 'the most advanced and capable radiation-hardened space processor in existence today'.

evidence.title: Breaking Defense: BAE rad-hard process nodes (150nm RAD750, 45nm RAD5545)
evidence.excerpt: The RAD750® computer is based on the 150-nanometer node. The RAD5545 computer is based on the newer and more advanced 45-nanometer node
evidence.summary: BAE's rad-hard SBC process nodes: RAD750 at 150nm, RAD5545 at 45nm; quoted by BAE Space Systems Lead Steve Russell.

evidence.title: Frontgrade Technologies — company description (largest rad-hard electronics provider)
evidence.excerpt: As the largest provider of analog and radiation-hardened electronics for the aerospace, defense, and medical industries
evidence.summary: Frontgrade self-describes as the largest provider of analog and rad-hard electronics; portfolio includes FPGAs, memory, and microprocessors. Vendor self-claim — needs an independent market-share source to promote a quantitative concentration figure.
evidence.limitations: Vendor self-claim of market leadership; no independent share figure. Frontgrade is private (Veritas Capital).

evidence.title: Microchip — RTG4 radiation-tolerant FPGAs (product page)
evidence.excerpt: resistant to radiation-induced configuration upsets in the harshest radiation environments, making them excellent options for use in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), Geostationary Equatorial Orbit (GEO), Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO) and deep-space flight applications.
evidence.summary: Microchip RTG4 rad-tolerant FPGAs hardened by design against single-event upsets across all orbital regimes; RT PolarFire is QML Class Q qualified.
evidence.limitations: Vendor product page; 'one of two dominant space-FPGA suppliers' framing is from secondary trade coverage, not a quantified share.

evidence.title: AMD IR — Class B qualification for first space-grade Versal adaptive SoCs
evidence.excerpt: AMD today announced it has completed Class B qualification for the company's first space-grade Versal adaptive SoCs.
evidence.summary: AMD completed Class B qualification of the XQR Versal AI Core XQRVC1902 (radiation-tolerant, reprogrammable in-flight), shipping from early 2023; the other dominant merchant space-FPGA line (with Microchip).

evidence.title: SkyWater Technology — DoD $99M to advance strategic rad-hard production
evidence.excerpt: Department of Defense (DOD) has awarded the company up to $99 million as a continuation of the previous initiative to broaden onshore production capabilities for strategic radiation-hardened (rad-hard) electronics.
evidence.summary: DoD funding to SkyWater (up to $99M, on top of an earlier up-to-$170M program) to broaden onshore strategic rad-hard (RH90) production capacity. From the .eval dev set; SkyWater is a DMEA Trusted Foundry.

evidence.title: SpaceX Falcon avionics — COTS silicon with radiation characterization (analysis)
evidence.excerpt: SpaceX's approach is to use commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) silicon with radiation characterization, acceptance testing, and architectural mitigation (error correction codes, watchdog timers, scrubbing routines) rather than paying the full rad-hard premium.
evidence.summary: Secondary engineering analysis of Falcon avionics: COTS silicon + radiation characterization + triple-string redundancy in place of strategic rad-hard parts. Supports the COTS-vs-rad-hard honesty split. The underlying redundancy architecture is corroborated by the SpaceX Falcon Users Guide (ev_space_falcon_users_guide_2025).
evidence.limitations: Secondary/blog analysis, not a SpaceX primary doc; treat as a pointer. The 'three-string fault-tolerant architecture' it quotes is from the Falcon Users Guide already in the graph.

evidence.title: Honeywell MIMU — ring-laser-gyro inertial unit for satellite and launch-vehicle programs
evidence.excerpt: Within the MIMU is a series of RLGs that measures changes in angular rotation; the accelerometers measure changes in linear acceleration.
evidence.summary: Honeywell MIMU is a ring-laser-gyro + accelerometer inertial measurement unit described as a small, lightweight measurement system for commercial and military satellite and launch-vehicle programs.
evidence.limitations: Heritage counts ('250th MIMU', >1M on-orbit hours) appear in secondary summaries of an older Honeywell press release that no longer resolves; not asserted here without a live primary source.

evidence.title: Military & Aerospace Electronics: Northrop HRG reaches 50M on-orbit hours
evidence.excerpt: Northrop Grumman Corporation's hemispherical resonator gyro (HRG) has reached 50 million operating hours in space without a single mission failure.
evidence.summary: Northrop SIRU/HRG inertial reference: 50M on-orbit hours with zero mission failures, aboard 200+ spacecraft, naturally radiation-hardened by its quartz construction. Second dominant space-IMU/gyro house.

evidence.title: Sodern — world leader in star trackers (product page)
evidence.excerpt: As the world leader in star trackers, Sodern offers the most extensive range of products on the market
evidence.summary: Sodern self-describes as world leader in star trackers (Hydra, Auriga) with extensive flight heritage from LEO to deep space. Vendor self-claim of leadership; a separate WebSearch summary cited 'over 1,500 units launched' but that figure was not on a directly-fetched page.
evidence.limitations: Vendor self-claim; quantitative '1,500 units / 30M hours' figure seen only in an aggregator summary, not asserted here.

evidence.title: Jena-Optronik — ASTRO APS most-used high-reliability attitude sensor
evidence.excerpt: The ASTRO APS is the world's most successful and extensively used high-reliability satellite attitude orbit control sensor.
evidence.summary: Jena-Optronik ASTRO APS described as the world's most successful high-reliability satellite attitude-orbit-control sensor; the compact rad-hard ASTRO CL targets small satellites and mega-constellations. Second established European star-tracker house. Subsidiary of Airbus Defence and Space.
evidence.limitations: Vendor self-claim of leadership; no independent share figure.

evidence.title: BAE Systems (Ball Aerospace) CT-2020 radiation-hardened star tracker
evidence.excerpt: The CT-2020 from BAE Systems is a Radiation-Hardened Star Tracker engineered for precise and reliable spacecraft attitude determination across a wide range of space missions.
evidence.summary: Ball Aerospace CT-2020 (now BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems after the 2024 acquisition) is a rad-hard star tracker for spacecraft attitude determination; third established star-tracker supplier.

evidence.title: Glenair — launch-vehicle avionics interconnect systems (space page)
evidence.excerpt: Whether the requirement is a miniature payload connector, a complete spacecraft harness architecture, a launch vehicle avionics interconnect system, or a precision deployment mechanism, Glenair delivers the connectors, cables, mechanisms, and engineering expertise required to connect and deploy mission-critical space systems.
evidence.summary: Glenair delivers complete launch-vehicle avionics interconnect systems with proven flight heritage across government, commercial, and defense space programs. Private company.

evidence.title: Glenair Mighty Mouse — de facto high-performance connector solution
evidence.excerpt: the high-performance Mighty Mouse is now specified on hundreds of mission-critical interconnect applications worldwide and has become the de facto high-performance connector solution for many former users of D38999.
evidence.summary: Glenair Series 80 Mighty Mouse is the de facto high-performance miniature connector on hundreds of mission-critical applications, at roughly half the size and weight of MIL-DTL-38999.
evidence.limitations: Vendor self-claim of de-facto status; qualitative, not a quantified share.

evidence.title: TE Connectivity — DEUTSCH space-qualified connectors
evidence.excerpt: The DEUTSCH DBAS series connectors deliver integrated, high-performance solutions for aerospace, military, and space applications. Both the DBAS 7 Series and DBAS 9 Series connectors are built for high-temperature, cryogenic, and pyrotechnic environments.
evidence.summary: TE Connectivity DEUTSCH DBAS connectors are space-qualified for high-temperature, cryogenic, pyrotechnic, and radiation-exposed launch/space environments. Second-source launch-harness candidate.

evidence.excerpt: Amphenol's VITA 78 SpaceVPX connectors leverage OpenVPX architecture and technology and are designed and tested for extreme space environments, including exposure to radiation, extreme temperatures and vibration.
